developer-tooling.title: Adopt OmniEngineering workspace and Headroom context optimization
developer-tooling.description: Install the OmniEngineering .ai/ scaffold and ./omni CLI so assistant sessions share one loading order, ruleset and requirements registry; install Headroom's Claude Code integration at local scope so tool output is compressed through the local proxy.
acceptance_criteria: python omni doctor reports only the known upstream gaps listed in .ai/project-configuration.md
.claude/settings.local.json carries the Headroom env and hooks and is git-ignored
risk_notes: No pristine OmniEngineering upstream is available locally; the scaffold was assembled from STEP-Migration copies, so .ai/adapters/, .ai/checklists/public-release.md, fallback-llm-rules.json and hci-ui-rules.json are absent
With Headroom routing enabled, Claude Code sessions in this repo depend on the local proxy on port 8787 being reachable

developer-tooling.title: Bound requirement registry growth with an archive lifecycle
developer-tooling.description: The active registry is loaded into every session by every context profile so unbounded growth is a permanent context tax rather than mere file bloat. Completed and withdrawn requirements are swept into an archive that no context profile loads while ids stay unique across both files.
acceptance_criteria: omni requirement archive moves terminal requirements out of the active registry
next_requirement_id never reuses an archived id
omni doctor errors when active and archived ids collide
archiving a requirement that is not completed or withdrawn is refused
risk_notes: make_ai.py is vendored OmniEngineering tooling so these changes must be reapplied if a pristine upstream is ever pulled

documentation.title: Restructure product documentation into an overview plus category documents
documentation.description: README.md had grown to 900 lines and served as the only product document. Split it into a professional overview covering capabilities and administration plus ten category documents under docs/ so granular material is found by type rather than by scrolling.
acceptance_criteria: README.md is an overview rather than a full manual
docs/ holds one document per category
no carried-forward claim is restated without checking it against source
risk_notes: Measured figures were carried forward from an earlier corpus run and are labelled as such until tools/corpus.py is rerun

training-evidence.title: Settle corpus composition figures and make them recomputable
training-evidence.description: Documentation quoted 42 repositories in one place and 39 in another while the population table mixed a tuned-only count for the vulnerable population with full counts for the other two. tools/corpus.py is authoritative: 41 repositories of which 5 are held out leaving a tuning set of 36.
acceptance_criteria: python tools/corpus.py --counts prints composition with nothing cloned
README.md and docs/evidence.md cite 41 total and 5 held out and 36 tuned
stack coverage gaps are reported directionally rather than as one merged list
risk_notes: The measured lines and findings table predates the two Go repositories added later and stays labelled until a corpus run refreshes it
